correctness.rationale: The chain-level sign calculation is exact for every invariant simplex, the orbit quotient is literally the same comb graph with one arm per permutation cycle, and the known all-parameter ordinary Euler recurrence supplies the two parity sequences. Signed ladder transfer independently verifies the even branch and a one-arm cancellation gives the odd branch. The n=2 integral claim combines the proven one-dimensional character with the established sphere homotopy type. A standalone exact-integer enumerator checked every graph simplex and 498 permutations in 18 cases; finite checks are corroboration rather than an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly poses the symmetric-group homology action as an open problem. The complete all-parameter, all-conjugacy-class alternating character identifies cancellation of all higher Specht constituents, and the n=2 result identifies the integral sign lattice, a previously unrecorded group-action invariant. This distinguishes multiple homology actions with the same known nonequivariant Euler and sphere data, providing a structural partial answer to the exact published research question.
